mathematical_definition: A Dedekind lower cut L⊂Q is a nonempty proper lower subset of the rational numbers with no greatest element: q∈L and p<q imply p∈L, and every q∈L has r∈L with q<r. The set of such cuts admits an order by inclusion; field arithmetic requires a further explicit construction.
source_variants: lower-subset cut with nonempty proper, lower closed, no maximum
ordered pair of lower and upper parts with partition and separation
mathematical_audit: ProofWiki's second paired-sets presentation should not be treated as automatically equivalent unless it also excludes empty/full degeneracies. When S=Q and L=∅, some written pair conditions can hold vacuously. An independent equivalence proof must check partition, nonemptiness and maximum conditions before equating the forms.

topic: Real numbers via rational Cauchy classes
mathematical_definition: Let C(Q) be the set of all rational Cauchy sequences. Define x∼y if |x_n−y_n|→0 as n→∞ in the rational absolute value, equivalently for every positive rational ε there exists N with n≥N implying |x_n−y_n|<ε. The real-number set may be constructed as equivalence classes C(Q)/∼ with induced addition and multiplication.
source_variants: Cauchy sequence equivalence classes of rationals
total order and addition induced from Cauchy representatives
mathematical_audit: The source uses the stronger-looking cross-index i,j≥N difference |x_i−y_j|<ε, which is equivalent when each input sequence is itself Cauchy. Without restricting to Cauchy inputs, this cross-index definition must not be conflated with ordinary sequencewise convergence to zero. Field operations/order must be proved well defined on classes; sequences themselves are not individual real numbers.

mathematical_definition: A real number may be represented by signed base-b positional expansions, where b≥2 and digit sequences may have distinct representations for the same number, such as 1.000…=0.999… in base ten. Therefore the bare set of all infinite digit strings is not literally the set of real numbers without identification and an explicit sign/integer-part convention.
source_variants: base-b positional expansion with signed integer part and fractional digits
quotient of expansions identifying terminating versus recurring maximal-digit tails
mathematical_audit: The article's digit-sequence formulation omits a rigorous resolution of signed reals and nonunique expansions; do not screen this as an equivalent bare-set definition until these issues and convergence interpretation are explicitly fixed.
